synthetic_polytrack.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise (left-handed). Positioned alongside the main turf course at Tynong. A state-of-the-art 2,000m synthetic oval that hosts intense winter racing. While more spacious than older synthetic tracks, it produces a grinding environment where kickback can be a factor. Tactical speed ('P') and rail-skimming trips hold a natural mathematical advantage over wide, sweeping runs.
synthetic_polytrack.post_bias: Inside barriers (stalls 1–4) hold a distinct advantage, particularly in 1000m, 1200m, and 1400m events. Being caught three-wide without cover on the synthetic surface bleeds crucial momentum.

handicapping_angles.synthetic_specialists_priority: Shift away from standard grass turn-of-foot metrics. Prioritize horses with proven synthetic records (Pakenham Polytrack, Ballarat Synthetic, Geelong Synthetic), high tactical gate speed, and deep fitness profiles.
handicapping_angles.grass_to_synthetic_transition_tax: Horses making their synthetic debut from pure turf backgrounds can struggle with footing and kickback unless possessing high 1st-call gate speed. Apply a -2.0 point discount to first-time synthetic starters with zero synthetic trials.
handicapping_angles.pakenham_winter_poly_fitness: During the Victorian winter (May to August), Pakenham Synthetic hosts frequent TAB cards. High-volume Victorian yards (Ciaron Maher, Busuttin/Young, Mick Price & Michael Kent Jr., Ben, Will & JD Hayes) dominate synthetic maiden and BM58 handicaps.
